01

Where every part of this edition comes from

Adapted from jekyll-theme-conference by Digitale Gesellschaft, MIT licensed, copyright 2017 to 2026 Lorenz Schmid. This is an adaptation, not an unchanged upstream theme: the structure was reused and the surface was written from scratch.

The foundation

jekyll-theme-conference, pinned at the commit below, MIT. Its notice is kept in the source archive at licenses/jekyll-theme-conference-MIT.txt, and the whole upstream repository at that commit ships inside the archive under upstream/.

7d7479e486d87c59a15280e20e76c015d26aabb1

The upstream repository

What was taken

The structure, which is the part worth having: a multi day programme laid out as a time grid with rooms across the top and time down the side, sessions placed by start time and duration, a track colour carried on the left edge, a track key under the grid, talk pages, a speaker index and room and venue pages, and one schedule data file that the grid is generated from.

What was not taken

Jekyll, Liquid, Bootstrap 5 and its colour utilities, the Bootstrap icon set, the Leaflet map on the location page, the dark mode switch, the live indication and stream modal, the progressive web app layer, the service worker, and every line of upstream copy. An edition that looked like Bootstrap would not be worth shipping.

What is new here

Every page, all the copy, the whole type system, the colour set, the CSS grid that replaces the upstream table, the responsive behaviour that turns the grid into a chronological list on a narrow screen, the day tabs and the track filter, and all six drawings.

Type

Space Grotesk for display, headings and every time on the site, under the SIL Open Font License. Inter for running text, under the same licence. Both are bundled as local files with their licences beside them. No font is fetched from anywhere.

Drawings

Six SVG files written by hand for this edition: the house mark, three track marks, the venue plan and the approach drawing. There are no photographs in this edition, no generated images, and nothing taken from any reference site.

Nothing remote

No scripts, fonts, analytics, maps, embeds or form services are loaded from anywhere. The venue page draws its own plan and its own approach instead of embedding a map. Contact is a mailto link with an example address.

The content

Plenum, its dates, its venue, its rooms, its thirty sessions and its twelve speakers are invented for this template. No real congress, no real person, no prices, no sponsors and no attendance figures appear anywhere.

02

Take the source

The complete adapted source ships beside the built pages: every page, the stylesheet, the script, the fonts, the drawings, the licences, the schedule data file and the tool that renders the grid from it, plus the pinned upstream.

Unpack the archive and open index.html through any static server. There is no build step. To change the schedule, edit tools/programme-data.json and run the grid tool with node; it rewrites the marked region of programme.html and the placement classes in style.css and leaves everything else alone.
